init.title: Kia Access options
init.description: By default every update reads the manufacturer's server-side cache, which is gentle on the car's 12V battery. Turn on 'Poll the car directly' only if you need up-to-the-minute data — it wakes the vehicle on every poll and can flatten the 12V battery if the car is parked for long periods.

data.poll_car_directly: Poll the car directly (wakes the vehicle — drains the 12V battery)
data.force_refresh_timeout: Live wake-up wait (seconds) — only used when polling directly
data.price_per_kwh: Price per kWh (your all-in marginal rate, 0 = no cost tracking)
data.range_factor: Range reach factor (haircut on the car's range estimate)
data.range_reserve_pct: Range reach reserve % (arrive with this much charge left)
data.calendar_entities: Calendar entities for trip destinations (comma-separated, e.g. calendar.work, calendar.family)
data.drive_time_max_routed: Destinations to route (rows on the MagicMirror panel)
data.alert_title: Alert title (blank = the vehicle's own default)

data_description.vin: Which vehicle this entry tracks. Required once the account has more than one vehicle (each needs its own config entry) — blank is fine for a single-vehicle account. Changing this moves the entry to a different vehicle; it's rejected if another Kia Access entry already uses that VIN.
data_description.scan_interval: How often Home Assistant asks the manufacturer's servers for a fresh reading.
data_description.stale_after_minutes: How old the CAR'S OWN last-reported reading can get before the data-stale sensor turns on — independent of the poll interval above, since a poll can succeed while the car itself hasn't reported in a while (parked, asleep, out of signal).
data_description.poll_car_directly: Off (recommended): data comes from the manufacturer's servers — refreshed whenever the car itself checks in (driving, charging, app use). On: each poll wakes the car for a live reading.
data_description.force_refresh_timeout: How long to wait for the car to answer before falling back to the cached copy for that poll.
data_description.price_per_kwh: Used to turn charge sessions into a running cost log. 0 disables cost tracking entirely (sessions are still logged in kWh).
data_description.capacity_kwh: Overrides the usable battery capacity used for range/cost-per-% calculations. 0 auto-detects from the vehicle's own reported values where available.
data_description.range_factor: Applied to the car's own range estimate before showing reachable destinations, to account for terrain/weather/driving-style optimism in the car's number.
data_description.range_reserve_pct: How much charge to still have left on arrival at a destination, before it's shown as reachable.
data_description.calendar_entities: Events with a location on these calendars are geocoded and added to the reachable-destinations list / range-map pins. Destinations more than ~500 km from zone.home are skipped as implausible.
data_description.calendar_lookahead_hours: How far ahead to look for upcoming calendar events when building the reachable-destinations list.
data_description.drive_time_provider: Estimate (default) uses straight-line distance. Geoapify or TomTom return real road distance and live-traffic drive time while the car is at home, within the call budget below (needs the matching API key).
data_description.routing_api_key: Used for live drive times AND for geocoding calendar event locations. A Geoapify key works for both even if the drive-time provider is left on “estimate” (Nominatim increasingly blocks Home Assistant).
data_description.drive_time_routes: TomTom only: one routing call per destination each refresh so the reachable list can show “via <roads>” and colour the ETA by traffic delay. Turn off for one matrix call instead (time + distance only; TomTom bills it per destination from a much smaller free allowance).
data_description.drive_time_interval_min: Live drive times are only fetched while the car is at home (zone.home). This is the minimum gap between refreshes during the day; a refresh also runs straight away when the car gets home. Away from home the list shows straight-line estimates (“~”).
data_description.drive_time_night_interval_min: Minimum gap between drive-time refreshes overnight (11pm–6am).
data_description.drive_time_max_routed: Only the destinations the MagicMirror panel shows are routed: your fixed destinations and picked zones first, then calendar events, soonest first, up to this many (match the panel's drivingTimes.max). Other rows use straight-line estimates. Each routed destination costs one call per refresh.
data_description.routing_monthly_budget: Hard cap on routing calls per calendar month (one per routed destination per refresh). What's left is spread evenly over the remaining days, so a busy week slows refreshes rather than running out. TomTom's free tier is 20,000 routing calls a month; Geoapify's is 3,000 credits a day.
data_description.panel_destinations: Places that always get a row on the MagicMirror driving-times panel; calendar events fill the remaining rows, soonest first. Pick zones from the list, or type a fixed destination as "Name | address" (e.g. "White House | 1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington, DC") and press Enter -- addresses are geocoded once and cached, and also appear in Home Assistant. Pick no zones to make every zone within ~500 km of zone.home eligible instead, but only after the calendar events. Type "-Name" to hide a zone. The Home Assistant dashboard and sensor always show every zone.
data_description.geocoding_api_key: A Geoapify key used only to turn calendar / static addresses into coordinates. Set this if your routing provider is TomTom (TomTom's Search API is not on every key) or you left the provider on “estimate”.
data_description.block_automated_climate: Reject start_climate / stop_climate unless the call comes straight from a person (the card, the button, Developer Tools, a script you run by hand). Automations, scripts triggered by automations, scenes and the preconditioning blueprints are blocked. Does not touch the car's own scheduled climate set in the manufacturer's app.
data_description.away_price_per_kwh: Rate for charge sessions that start outside the home-charging zone (public chargers). 0 = fall back to the home rate.
data_description.currency: A label only, shown as the unit on the cost sensors (e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP") -- your price-per-kWh rates are already in this currency, nothing is converted.
data_description.home_charge_zone: The zone that counts as “home” for charging costs — e.g. zone.home, or a dedicated zone around your charger. Leave blank to cost every session at the home rate.
data_description.charge_rates: Different $/kWh per charging location, one per line as "zone.work = 0.19" (or "Work = 0.19"). When the car charges inside one of these zones that rate is used and the session is filed under that zone name; the first matching line wins. Zones not listed fall back to the away, then the home rate. A line for your home zone (labelled “home”) keeps that session in the home bucket.
data_description.away_cost_entity: A sensor whose value is the cost of your latest public charge — e.g. from the ChargePoint or a Tesla HA integration. When an away session ends and this sensor reported a figure within its window, that becomes the session cost (the rate estimate is kept as estimated_cost). Otherwise the away $/kWh rate is used.
data_description.away_cost_grace_min: How long after unplugging the away cost sensor may still update — public networks often bill a few minutes to an hour later.
data_description.charger_status_entity: A home charger's own charging-status entity — e.g. ChargePoint's binary_sensor.<charger>_charging, or Emporia's status sensor (ha-emporia-ev). When set, Kia Access sends a 'Charging started' alert the moment this turns on, and a 'Charging stopped' alert when it turns off, with the energy used and its cost at your configured rate. Works the same regardless of which charger integration the entity comes from.
data_description.charger_energy_entity: The home charger's own energy sensor (kWh) — e.g. ChargePoint's session_energy_kwh or Emporia's usage sensor. Sampled at charge start and stop; the difference is reported as the session's energy in the 'Charging stopped' alert. Leave blank to get the start/stop alerts without an energy or cost figure.
data_description.charger_power_entity: The home charger's own live power sensor (W) — e.g. Emporia's Power sensor. Some chargers keep reporting "charging" on their status entity until a scheduled session end, well after the car actually stopped drawing current; when set, the 'Charging stopped' alert reports the duration and finish time from the last moment power was genuinely flowing, not the status entity's own end time. Purely informational — it never starts, stops, or duplicates an alert on its own, so a brief top-off blip after the battery's full just moves this later, it can't cause an extra start/stop pair.
data_description.alert_title: Shown as the notification title for kia_access_alert events. Blank uses a generic default — set this if you'd like it to name your specific vehicle or brand.
data_description.quiet_while_driving: Hold back warning/info alerts (door open, low 12V, etc.) while the car is moving, and deliver them once it's parked. Critical alerts always fire immediately.

data.price_per_kwh: Price per kWh (your all-in marginal rate, 0 = no cost tracking)
